title: Local vanishing of affine-line supported restriction at a zero germ
statement:
Fix a finite purity setting $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], with coefficient ring $A$, positive level $n$ and $h:e(P)\mid n$. Let $a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type, and let $s:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$ be the zero section. Write $G=Rs^!A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ for the actual finite exceptional value of [lem-pur-gysin-structure]. Let $D$ be normalized support data of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], so $D.\mathrm{support}:\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2_{s(Y)}(\mathbf A^1_Y,A(1))$ is its specified chart. Let $H$ be an etale sheaf of $A$-modules and $e:\nu_Y^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0G$. For a map $b:A_{Y,\mathrm{et}}\to H$, let $v_b=\operatorname{ev}_1(\nu_Y^*b\mathbin{\gg}e)$, using the evaluation of [lem-pur-gysin-structure]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed $k$-field in the scheme universe. The symbol $1_y$ denotes the canonical germ of $1$ in the constant-sheaf stalk, as in [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. Let $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Let $p$ be any normalized supported-pair transport for the induced affine-line square, as defined by [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback], and write $r_y^p$ for its actual kernel-derived restriction with the canonical coefficient pullback of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Then, for every $b:A_{Y,\mathrm{et}}\to H$,
$$b_y(1_y)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad r_y^p(D.\mathrm{support}(v_b))=0.$$
No finite-type condition is imposed on $\Omega$, and $y$ need not respect its given $k$-algebra structure.

source.place: Step 2: supported restriction is stalkwise evaluation. Its zero-germ consequence is the local-vanishing/excision step: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 9, Theorems 9.4 and 9.7, and Example 9.5.

proof.text: A linear map from the constant-sheaf stalk is determined by 1. Thus b_y is zero. The identity stalk on Spec Omega is faithful, since constants and global sections are inverse equivalences and constant-sheaf stalks recover the coefficient module. The pullback/stalk isomorphism gives y_et^*(b)=0. This can also be witnessed on a pointed etale neighbourhood by filtered-colimit equality.

Use the Hom-to-sections bijection of [lem-pur-gysin-structure] to lift the evaluated section to m:A_Y[0] -> G. The two adjunction Hom equivalences defining evaluation, together with determination of a linear map from A by 1, show that H0(m) is nu(b) followed by e. Exact coherent comparison makes its geometric pullback zero. Concentration of G in degree zero and the fully faithful single-complex embedding then show that the derived pullback of m is zero.

Evaluation on 1 identifies ordinary Hom from the constant coefficient sheaf with global sections, naturally. Derive this additive identification and use [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] to identify global hypercohomology with derived Hom from the constant, with its cocycle roof formula. At the specified compactification (id,s), the class adjunction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], with its bounded-below etale antecedents, represents the finite exceptional Hom functor as Hom from the etale supported constant shifted by minus two. The normalized supported-Hom identification and site transport in [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] give the same representation for the actual support group. In these coordinates the natural supportIso of [lem-pur-retracted-support-localization-comparison] is a natural automorphism of a representable functor, so Yoneda expresses it as precomposition with an endomorphism t. The normalized cocycle formula for edge and the equations edge_spec and support_spec identify the displayed D.support class with the image of the canonical adjoint of m under this support comparison. It is enough to preserve zero pullback; no formula for t is required.

Lift m to the retained bounded-below etale antecedents. Coherent comparison and faithfulness carry its zero pullback to them. Write the ordinary closed-adjoint transpose as S(m) followed by the counit. The naturality square of the finite closed direct-image exchange in [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] rewrites its pullback, precomposed with that invertible exchange, as S applied to the zero pulled-back m, followed by the pulled-back counit. Thus the pulled-back transpose is zero. Precomposition by the fixed t from step 3 preserves this zero. Only ordinary closed direct-image exchange is inverted; no exceptional base-change isomorphism is assumed.

The supported-Hom pullback equation and coefficient naturality identify this zero Hom with the actual derived kernel restriction and orientationInputPullback. The arbitrary normalized transport p gives the same restriction: its terminal arrow is unique over the pullback of the identity, supportUnit_spec and the monic kernel inclusion determine its support unit, and deriving preserves this equality. Injectivity of the target supported-Hom identification proves the conclusion. The argument includes disconnected and empty bases, the zero ring, and geometric fields not of finite type.

proof_origin.place: Source Step 2, its zero-germ consequence. Use degree-zero concentration and the canonical closed adjoint, with Yoneda naturality preserving zero pullback; Milne Section 9 functoriality.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf section with zero geometric germ vanishes on an etale neighbourhood, and its cohomology class restricts to zero on the geometric fibre
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits, headed by RingedSpace.exists_res_eq_zero_of_germ_eq_zero. These concern Zariski structure-sheaf germs and do not identify the normalized Gysin supported restriction.

12 generic point-fibre colimit and naturality lemmas, including toPresheafFiber, toPresheafFiber_naturality and toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberDesc. They construct germs but do not identify the finite exceptional support chart.
17 hits, mostly structure-sheaf or ringed-space germs. No etale Gysin supported restriction compatibility.

mathlib_searches.query: A section of an etale sheaf with zero geometric germ has zero restriction to supported cohomology on that geometric fibre
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.res_zero, TopCat.Presheaf.Γgerm_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext, AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_res_eq_zero_of_germ_eq_zero, AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.zero_apply, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zero_of_zero_cover, AlgebraicGeometry.exists_of_res_zero_of_qcqs, AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_basicOpen_eq_zero_of_isCompact. The returned declarations concern ordinary topological or structure-sheaf germs and restrictions. None identifies the actual Gysin supported restriction with a geometric germ.

theorem affineLine_support_restriction_zero_germ (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (h : P.ramificationIndex ∣ P.level) (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (a : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k))
    [IsSeparated a] [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a]
    (D : OrientationSupportData P h Y)
    (H : ProEtale.RetractedSupport.EtSheaves P Y)
    (e : (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) Y).obj H ≅
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ProEtale.RetractedSupport.ProSheaves P Y) 0).obj (P.gysinValue h Y))
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra P.field.k Ω]
    (y : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ Y)
    (p : proEtaleSupportHomTransport P (zeroSection Y)
      (zeroSection (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω))) (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) y))
    (b : P.constantEtale Y ⟶ H)
    (hb : ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber.map b)
      (((Scheme.pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiberConstantSheafIso
        (ModuleCat.of P.Coefficient P.Coefficient)).inv 1) = 0) :
    P.orientationSupportRestriction h y p
      (D.support.hom (P.gysinEvaluate Y
        ((ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) Y).map b ≫
          e.hom))) = 0
